messages:
tyler_sales: Quick ask from Nimbus: they want a nightly CI job that pulls a hosted POC key, rotates it, and can hit a single revoke API if they spot suspicious activity. Looking for recommended API pattern and an example GH Actions step. @anika_se @omar_infra

anika_se: We should give them a bootstrap-token -> exchange flow. Bootstrap token short TTL (1h) created via console or API. CI exchanges it for an ephemeral hosted key (6-12h TTL). For nightly rotate, CI calls exchange then calls revoke on previous key_id once new key is stored.

omar_infra: API endpoints we expose: POST /v1/bootstrap-tokens (create), POST /v1/token-exchange (bootstrap->hosted), POST /v1/keys/revoke, POST /v1/keys/rotate (atomic). We can support rotate with previous_key_id to auto-revoke. Recommend enabling IP allowlist and scope locks (generate,embeddings).

cale_ops: Ops considerations: add webhook callback on revoke and rotate events so their security team gets immediate confirmation. Also include an audit_reason field on revoke for SSO audit trails. Retain associated logs for 90 days.

tyler_sales: They also want a UI button in our console to revoke a key and optionally generate a replacement. Is that doable quickly?

omar_infra: Yes, console action maps to POST /v1/keys/rotate with auto_revoke=true. We can add confirmation modal and require a reason for SSO-linked accounts. For tenants wanting full automation, they can call the rotate API directly from CI with the bootstrap token flow.

anika_se: I'll draft a 1-page runbook with the curl samples and a GH Actions snippet. Sample snippet for GH Actions: 
```yaml
- name: Exchange bootstrap token for hosted key
  run: |
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference/v1/token-exchange \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"bootstrap_token":"${{ secrets.BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN }}","ci_worker":"nightly-runner"}' > key.json
    export HOSTED_KEY=$(jq -r .key key.json)
    # store to secret manager here
```

cale_ops: Small note: CI should confirm new key works before revoking old one. Also set short TTLs so orphaned keys expire fast.

tyler_sales: Awesome. Please post the runbook + sample console screenshots and I'll forward to Nimbus. They also asked about immediate revocation effect: will in-flight requests fail?

omar_infra: Revocation takes effect at the next auth check; any requests already validated will continue until token check happens (stateless checks use key id revocation cache which is updated within seconds). Not ideal to guarantee 0-in-flight usage, but effectively immediate for our purposes. We can also rotate to a fallback service account if they need continuity.
